(Updates with index/price moves and economic/geopolitical news from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes traded mixed as investors awaited quarterly earnings from Microsoft (MSFT) and Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) after the Federal Reserve left monetary policy unchanged for October.

The S&P 500 climbed 0.1% to 7,730.9, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.1% to 52,431.3 ahead of Wednesday's close. The Nasdaq Composite edged down 0.1% to 26,448.5. Energy and healthcare were top gainers. Real estate and utilities led decliners.

The Federal Open Market Committee maintained the target rate for federal funds at 3.75% to 4.00%, saying it would like more information before acting, an FOMC statement Wednesday afternoon showed. "The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2% goal."

Two dissents to the vote to maintain the policy rate were from Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, who both preferred a 25-basis-point rate increase at this meeting.

US Treasury yields were mixed, with rates on maturities below five years declining while those above jumped. The two-year yield fell 2.1 basis points to 4.72%, after rising earlier in the session. The 10-year rate advanced 4.1 basis points to 5.05%.

The US has asked several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the midterm elections, people briefed on the conversations told The Wall Street Journal. President Donald Trump said "anything is possible" when reporters asked about a possible attack on Iran after the US midterms, Al Jazeera, a Middle Eastern broadcaster, reported.

Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said any Israeli "military misadventure" in the Gulf region could have a "devastating impact" on global energy markets, Al Jazeera reported.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract jumped 2.8% to $102.68 per barrel, and global benchmark Brent climbed 1.2% to $115.20 per barrel.

Mag-7 duo Microsoft and Alphabet are expected to report their fiscal Q1 and Q3 financial results, respectively, after the market closes on Wednesday.

title: Down 82% from all-time highs, can PayPal stock finally recover in 2027?
detail:
Down 82% from all-time highs, can PayPal stock finally recover in 2027?
Aditya Raghunath
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 4:09 PM EDT 6 min read
PYPL
^GSPC
Trade PYPL on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Valued at a market cap of $47 billion, PayPal has grossly underperformed the broader markets over the last five years. Today, the fintech giant trades 82% below all-time highs, while the S&P 500 index is close to record levels. 

The ongoing drawdown has meant that PYPL stock trades at 10x forward earnings, below the 65x multiple in early 2021, given data from TIKR.

On Oct. 27, CEO Enrique Lores and Chief Financial and Operating Officer Jamie Miller gave investors their best evidence yet that a turnaround is taking shape. 

The question is whether that evidence is enough to lift the stock in 2027.

I have my doubts about the timing. Let me explain why.

Why PayPal stock lost its shine

PayPal built its name on online checkout. Shoppers trusted it with their payment details, which turned the PayPal button into a habit that powered the whole business.

Also Read: PayPal just lost its $53 billion safety net

Lores said on the company's Q3 earnings call that branded checkout volume has grown just 1% to 2% for four quarters in a row.  Miller added that the removal of the EU de minimis tax exemption created about 70 basis points of headwind. 

When a flagship product stalls, investors start to doubt everything built around it. 

So how does PayPal restart growth? Lores's plan is to stop leaning on checkout alone. He said the company now runs as three businesses with clearer accountability. 

He also said financial services already make up more than 20% of transaction margin dollars in 2026, and it's growing at double-digit rates.

Q3 shows early progress

PayPal managed to beat its own estimates in Q3 of 2026. Miller said transaction margin dollars came in above expectations, while operating expenses landed below forecast, helping drive earnings growth. 

Here are the numbers, according to PayPal's earnings call:

Transaction margin dollars rose about 2%, or 3% excluding interest on customer balances.

Non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) grew 8% to $1.45, above guidance.

Adjusted free cash flow came in at $2 billion.

PayPal bought back $1.5 billion of stock, bringing the trailing 12 months total to $6 billion.

Management then raised its full-year outlook.

It now expects transaction margin dollars of about $15.7 billion and non-GAAP EPS of about $5.60. Adjusted free cash flow is projected to reach $6.5 billion. 

Venmo and Pay Later carry the load

Checkout still drives most of PayPal's business, but it is not where the growth is.

Venmo is leading the way, with volume growing at a double-digit pace for eight straight quarters, according to Miller.

US equity indexes ended higher Wednesday after the Federal Reserve decided to maintain policy rates despite rising inflation.

* The Federal Reserve voted Wednesday to keep the overnight funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%, with two of the 12 members of the Federal Open Market Committee dissenting in favor of a quarter-percentage-point increase.

* The US has asked several Gulf Arab countries to be prepared for a short, intense military campaign after the midterm elections, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people briefed on the conversations.

* December West Texas Intermediate crude oil rose $2.71 to $102.61 per barrel, while December Brent crude, the global benchmark, was last seen up $1.18 at $115.06.

* Vertiv (VRT) shares rose nearly 17%, the top gainer on the S&P 500, after the company reported Q3 adjusted earnings and revenue above market expectations.

* F5 (FFIV) shares were down more than 20%, the worst performer on the S&P 500, after the company announced fiscal Q4 results and unveiled plans with Oracle (ORCL) to bring web application and API protection to customers running applications on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure under a non-binding memorandum of understanding.

title: How major US stock indexes fared Wednesday 10/28/2026
detail:
How major US stock indexes fared Wednesday 10/28/2026
The Associated Press
Wed, October 28, 2026 at 4:20 PM EDT 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^RUT
^IXIC

The bond market swung, while U.S. stocks held relatively steady after the Federal Reserve decided not to raise its main interest rate to bring down high inflation.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3% Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.2%, and the Nasdaq composite rose 0.3%.

In the bond market, the two-year Treasury yield initially jumped after the Fed held its main interest rate steady. It then reversed course after traders pared expectations for coming hikes to rates. Higher rates can help get high inflation under control, but they can also hurt the economy.

On Wednesday:

The S&P 500 rose 21.38 points, or 0.3%, to 7,743.98.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 97.53 points, or 0.2%, to 52,475.10.

The Nasdaq composite rose 72.04 points, or 0.3%, to 26,549.85.

The Russell 2000 rose 11.64 points, or 0.4%, to 2,830.51.

For the week:

The S&P 500 is up 120.30 points, or 1.6%.

The Dow is up 259.94 points, or 0.5%.

The Nasdaq is up 594.51 points, or 2.3%.

The Russell 2000 is up 54.61 points, or 2%.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 898.48 points, or 13.1%.

The Dow is up 4,411.81 points, or 9.2%.

The Nasdaq is up 3,307.86 points, or 14.2%.

The Russell 2000 is up 348.60 points, or 14%.
